release_notes: Working-analyzer release: the tables become instruments and the PHP tracking client grows up. Every data table in the panel (Campaigns, Offers, Landings, Logs, Conversions, the campaign report and the report customizer) gets drag-to-resize columns via one shared ColumnResize module — widths persist per table and restore to default, live during the drag; the load-bearing detail is overflow:hidden on the resize handle's header cell, without which the sticky header paints over the neighbouring handle. Click Log and Conversions Log move into proper modals (ClickLogModal keeps the cloak quick-filters ALL/SAFE/MONEY and the W1/W2 detail fields), reachable from both the Campaigns list and the stream cards in the campaign editor; campaign URLs are built by one shared campaignUrl helper; the Campaigns table gains a Domain column (api.php now joins domains on campaign_id). kclient.php 2.0: on secondary pages of the same site restoreFromQuery() picks the click back up from _subid and restores THIS click's offer from the session (id-matched, so a stale session can't hand over another click's offer), getOffer(42) keeps working in the bare-id form the integration panel documents, and choosing a specific offer now REPLACES the tracker's own offer_id on the transition link instead of appending a second one; the panel snippet is one paste-ready block with the alternatives commented beside it (Keitaro style), a secondary-page snippet and an offer-link helper are exported, and a new docs/tracking-client-php.md page is linked from the integration panel. KClient-arrived visitors get the full macro set on the direct destination path: {subid}, {ip} and {country} are substituted exactly like the campaign-link path, so an offer URL written with {subid} (the spelling most networks ask for) no longer reaches the network empty and the conversion postback has its click. The rotation optimiser stops cost-gating EPC — earnings per click has no spend term, so EPC configs now run on zero-cost campaigns (only ROI still requires cost); pinned in both the allocator and cron tests. Test-suite hygiene: four stale tests aligned with shipped behavior (TikTok resolveEvent's pixel-first signature, unknown postback statuses recording for retroactive mapping instead of a 400, DNS/nginx regression tests skipping on hosts without the fixtures) — the whole suite runs green.
